original_value: Compilers should not crash and they should not miscompile applications. Random testing is an effective method for finding compiler bugs that have escaped other kinds of testing. This paper presents Yet Another Random Program Generator (YARPGen), a random test-case generator for C and C++ that we used to find and report more than 220 bugs in GCC, LLVM, and the Intel® C++ Compiler. Our research contributions include a method for generating expressive programs that avoid undefined behavior without using dynamic checks, and generation policies, a mechanism for increasing diversity of generated code and for triggering more optimizations. Generation policies decrease the testing time to find hard-to-trigger compiler bugs and, for the kinds of scalar optimizations YARPGen was designed to stress-test, increase the number of times these optimizations are applied by the compiler by an average of 20% for LLVM and 40% for GCC. We also created tools for automating most of the common tasks related to compiler fuzzing; these tools are also useful for fuzzers other than ours.

result.paraphrase: Compilers should neither crash nor miscompile programs. Random testing is an effective way to uncover compiler bugs that other testing methods miss. This paper introduces Yet Another Random Program Generator (YARPGen), a random test-case generator for C and C++ that we used to discover and report more than 220 bugs in GCC, LLVM, and the Intel® C++ Compiler. Our contributions include a technique for generating expressive programs without undefined behavior and without dynamic checks, plus generation policies that increase the diversity of generated code and trigger more optimizations. These policies reduce the time needed to find hard-to-trigger compiler bugs and, for the scalar optimizations YARPGen was built to stress-test, raise how often the compiler applies them by an average of 20% in LLVM and 40% in GCC. We also developed tools that automate most common compiler-fuzzing tasks, and they are useful for fuzzers beyond ours.
